When testing the new bio feature  in-game, I came across a situation where the automatic censorship filtering erroneously "fixes" a bio. 

This is reproducible using these steps:

1) Write a bio
2) Somewhere in the bio, add the word "shit".
3) You will see that it gets converted to "poop".
4) Try Changing "poop" to "sh1t" (Use a '1' instead of an i).
5) The bio now has lost all of its formatting, capitalization, and spacing.

See images below for a before and after. This likely isn't a client issue but rather server-side, specifically the censorship script breaking when trying to parse "workaround-swears". I noticed that the '4' in "4-year veteren" got turned into an 'a', leading me to believe the issue lies in the string sanitization.

We fixed "amazing" a while ago! Thank you for the report.

If you come across other cases like this, please let us know!

"G↋n" still gets mangled. And judging from below, many other cases of this sort of mangling have been reported. So closing the ticket just because "amazing" was fixed is a bit premature. This ticket isn't resolved until the filtering is removed, IMO.

@{5a4b034d1ab4366d42644996|full_name} This canny wasn't really clear and focused, especially regarding the sentence 'You are amazing'. Technically, it has been completed. However, I believe we need clarification about how the censoring system works. If it is by design, we could make a feature request so the system could be more transparent to the end user, for example it can display an error message "This bio contains forbidden words" instead of messing the whole bio.

Thanks for speaking up! Like @{60c0e22718009c104862d5bc|full_name} said, it's more helpful if each Canny request focuses on a specific issue. Otherwise, user votes would become less useful.

@{5a4b034d1ab4366d42644996|full_name} - The text you posted contains the character "TURNED DIGIT THREE", Unciode character U+218B.

It's a duodecimal digit in math. I think unusual Unicode characters are often filtered for security reasons, or because it would be too difficult for VRChat to support every Unicode character.

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} it did focus on a single issue, until VRC staff merged several other word filter failure reports into this one, including general ones that aren't about a specific word, such as "Bio Censor Filter Removes Spaces, Capitalization, and Formatting when changing Bio In-game"

@{6219f63f55639e536dc83162|full_name} I opened a follow up Canny that is more focusing on the profanity filter system here:

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/profanity-filter-improvements

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} Well, _supporting_ every Unicode character - not so hard, just stop blocking them. I've worked for a company as a developer in a context where we had to support internationalised text of all kinds before - it isn't impossible, it's just hard. Competent developers can do it. Do VRChat hire any?

_Rendering_ every Unicode character, somewhat harder.

Note that "supporting" and "rendering" are not the same thing. If you show the character as a square box, that can be considered supporting it correctly. Solving the problem of having a font which contains the character is a next step thing. Not showing the character at all, or filtering it out, is just incorrect behaviour.

Nonetheless it's a character I have in all my bios everywhere else, but VRChat is unnecessarily blocking it. Whether you personally consider it worth using or not is sort of irrelevant - it's already in use, by me, right now, pretty everywhere other than VRChat.

And no, "security reasons" has never been, and will never be, an acceptable reason for having bad internationalisation in an application.

At least you have done the research, though. Turned digit 3 (↋) is indeed used to mean "eleven" in dozenal circles. That is exactly the meaning I have used it for in "G↋n" - the digit eleven stands in for omitting the middle eleven digits of "Globalisation".
